Great — thanks for the intro, Samantha. Quick technical checklist from our side to make the kickoff productive: 

1) Sample data & prompts: please share a small representative set (≈200 queries) and a higher-throughput set (≈2k queries) if possible. Include any PII/redaction rules.
2) Payload shape: typical request size (tokens per request), avg and max context lengths.
3) Network & access: preferred method (S3 presigned, SFTP, or an upload link). If S3, we'll provide a role/ARN for temporary read access.
4) Success criteria: any hard blockers (e.g., disallow external network calls from the runtime) or must-have behaviors.
5) Benchmark targets: latency P50/P95, throughput (rps), and expected concurrency during peak windows.

What I'll run in the kickoff: brief architecture alignment (how Redwood routes and isolates inference), an overview of evaluation plan (models + quantization profiles we'll test), and an initial perf/load run. Dev will lead correctness/regression checks against your prompt set.

Proposed timeslot: Thursday 10:30 PT works for me — I've tentatively penciled it. If that falls through, Friday morning is fine too.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

Thanks team — looking forward to today's session. A few concrete asks so we can scope the evaluation and produce an actionable MAP: 

- Can you confirm whether the eval should run against open models only or if we should include a Redwood-verified model variant (we often test both for perf/cost tradeoffs)?
- Please share a minimal schema for any chat/message fields (e.g., role/name/content) and a sample JSON payload for the nightly batch embedding job.
- For the perf tests, do you have a preferred concurrency pattern (steady rps vs ramp + sawtooth)? We'll use your preference to create a reproducible test harness.

Proposed evaluation plan (short):
1) Day 0 (kickoff): align scope, grant access to sample data.
2) Day 1–3: functional correctness runs (Dev leads) + small scale perf sanity checks.
3) Day 4–7: full perf runs with target concurrency and cost estimates.
4) Day 8–10: final report (latency percentiles, token costs, recommended config), and a recommendation for production rollout (dedicated vs shared).

I'll bring a simple test harness and sample scripts to the call; we can drop those in the Drive folder afterwards. If you have a sandbox cluster we can hit (VPC peering or allowlisted IP), that'd speed full-scaled tests; otherwise we can spin up a dedicated evaluation pool.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
